_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Check an AI-built app for leaks and open data...

description: Checks an app made with an AI app builder (Lovable, Bolt, v0, Replit, Cursor) for leaks and launch readiness. Use it when the user asks "is my Lovable app secure?", "is my Supabase data public?", "which security headers is my app missing?" or "is my app ready to launch?". For any public app it returns 8 security headers with the lines for the detected host, launchList: 20 of 160 launch items read from outside, each pass, fail or warn with a fix (checklist true adds the owner-only items), and shipNaked: 7 pre-launch pages (privacy policy naming each service, liability terms, cookie banner, deletion, refund line at checkout, legal contact, frontend keys) with text to paste. The first call also returns ownership_not_proven with a DNS TXT record or file: once published, the next call adds exposed files (.env, .git), masked keys in its JavaScript, source maps, open Supabase or Firebase data, and backend signals. GET only; database checks read status codes and row counts, never a row's data, and never write. Do not use it beyond the public checks on an app the user does not own, for private addresses, or to scan many sites.

checklist.description: true also returns the launch list items only the owner can check, each with how to check it (about 127 lines). Default false: only their count.

url.description: The app's address, such as https://my-app.lovable.app/ or myapp.com. Headers and the public launch items are checked for any public app; the full check needs the owner to publish a proof token on that host first.

name: ai_app_check

findings.description: Every confirmed problem, most severe first, each with the exact fix.

headerFix.description: Every missing header line in one paste-ready block for the detected host.

launchList.description: The launch list items that can be read from outside, in list order, each with pass, fail, warn or not_checked and the fix. ownerChecks is the count of items only the owner can check, or the items with how to check each when checklist is true.

shipNaked.description: The 7 pre-launch pages an AI-built app usually ships without (privacy policy naming every service, terms limiting liability, cookie banner, account deletion, refund line next to checkout, legal contact, no secret key in the frontend), each pass, fail, warn or not_checked; a fail or warn carries snippet, the text to paste.

verdict.description: exposed: a high or medium finding. clean: none, and nothing left to verify. unknown: none found, but needsVerification or notChecked holds something to check by hand, or the page did not answer. ownership_not_proven: the header results are complete; publish the record or file in publish and call again for the rest.

title: Check an AI-built app for leaks and open data
